content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"List the project documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any documents relevant to humidity ageing/transparency and simulation assumptions. Extract the three allowed radiator candidates, their permitted/meaningful thickness considerations if stated, and their 10-year-equivalent humidity transparency-loss values."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard non-simulation constraints: discard any candidate whose 10-year-equivalent humidity transparency loss exceeds 10%, and keep only candidates usable within the 1–6 cm thickness range. Record the numeric humidity-loss values for all candidates if possible."},{"id":"s3","description":"For each remaining candidate, run simulate_separation at representative thicknesses across the allowed 1–6 cm range, including at least 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 cm unless the documents specify a narrower valid range. Record all numeric pion/kaon separation results."},{"id":"s4","description":"Refine around the best-performing thickness for each viable candidate by simulating additional nearby thickness values as needed, prioritizing any region where the separation is near or above the 3.5 sigma requirement and any apparent optimum. Record the refined numeric separation results."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all viable candidate/thickness combinations using the hard requirements first: separation at 10 GeV/c must be at least 3.5 sigma and humidity transparency loss must be at most 10%. Among combinations satisfying both, identify the one with the highest simulated pion/kaon separation and record its radiator identifier, thickness, separation, and transparency-loss values numerically where possible."}]}

Radiator-R2 also passes separation at its optimum but is lower, and Radiator-R1 does not reach 3.5 sigma.
